comparison: Both evaluate IGF-1 association claims (C14-C17, C19, C60) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes failure to survive multiple testing correction and suspicious confidence intervals. Peer reviewers explicitly state Bonferroni correction yields non-significant results and criticize lack of false discovery rate control across 657 markers, making conclusions 'unreliable.'

Both evaluate testosterone and SHBG null findings (C18, C23-C28) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds consistent null results with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept these findings and request more extensive discussion, noting 'This is another trial finding no association of sex hormones to COVID-19.'

Both address BMI sensitivity analysis (C73-C75) but diverge: OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting consistent effect directions strengthen robustness. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating methods 'did not adequately address potential data confounders' including BMI and dexamethasone treatment, questioning sufficiency of the adjustment.

Both evaluate gene-region SNP sensitivity analysis (C82-C84) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes effect estimates closer to null suggest weak instrument bias. Peer reviewers express concern about weak instruments and 'large confidence intervals,' though they don't specifically comment on this particular sensitivity analysis.

Both address estradiol findings (C76-C81). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to extremely wide confidence intervals and single-SNP weak instrument bias. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, grouping with other null sex hormone findings and not challenging validity, though requesting expanded discussion.

Both evaluate biological plausibility claims (C29-C40) but strongly diverge: OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting well-documented mechanisms from prior literature. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, fundamentally challenging relevance since 'None of the markers were directly measured' and questioning mechanism discussion without direct measurements.

Both evaluate testosterone literature discussion (C46-C54, C86-C87) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of contradictory findings consistent with null results. Peer reviewers explicitly requested this expanded discussion of negative results, stating it should be discussed 'more extensively.'

Both evaluate methodological limitations discussion (C55-C57) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitations and MR strengths. Peer reviewers accept the general MR principle but raise specific implementation concerns about 'winner's curse' and whether limitations were adequately addressed.

Partial overlap on methodological claims (C7-C10, C63). OpenEval rates all methodology SUPPORTED with large sample sizes and well-documented instruments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, criticizing methods section for lacking details on LD clumping procedures and questioning examination of 657 markers without multiple testing correction.

Partial overlap on data sources and sample sizes (C11-C13, C61-C62, C85). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting appropriate documentation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'large cohort which adds to robustness,' though raising concerns about confounders within these cohorts.

Partial overlap on hospitalization claims (C20-C22). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to multiple testing failure and suspicious confidence intervals. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about bias handling including 'winner's curse and potential pleiotropy,' questioning whether biases were adequately addressed.

Partial overlap on limitations (C58-C59). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the limitation statement about generalizability constraints without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates IGF-1 and estrogen mechanistic interactions (C41-C45) as SUPPORTED based on well-documented literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background mechanism claims.

OpenEval evaluates background/rationale claims (C1-C6) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate literature citations establishing scientific rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory context claims.
